name: Laundry packets and cleaning products

6-12m.rationale: Sources give no age split within 5 and younger; crawling babies can reach low cabinets, so scored moderately.

12-24m.rationale: AAP calls laundry packets extremely toxic; no finer age data found, so scored conservatively.

24-36m.rationale: Same toxicity and same age-data limit.

36-60m.rationale: Included in the 5-and-younger poison center reports; older children can follow label instructions.

injury_evidence.note: U.S. poison centers received 1,423 reports of laundry packet exposures in children 5 and younger in those two months. AAP says exposures have slightly decreased since voluntary standards in 2015 but the products remain extremely toxic.

injury_evidence.cause_category: laundry packet injuries treated in emergency departments
injury_evidence.age_band: children under 5 (report scope; age of the product table not restated, so confirm)
injury_evidence.note: CPSC's annual pediatric poisoning report lists laundry packets at about 2,900 emergency-department-treated injuries in 2022 and bleach at about 2,700.

why_it_matters: Laundry packets and cleaners can badly harm a child who bites, swallows or gets them in the eyes. Locking them away, high up, reduces the risk.

fix_steps.text: Move laundry packets, detergent and cleaning products to a high cabinet out of sight and reach, not on top of the washer or dryer or in drawers beneath it.
Keep products in their original labeled containers, closed tightly, and leave packets in the original container until just before they go in the machine.
Keep the laundry room door closed when you are not in it, clean up spills right away, and never mix cleaning products.
Add a cabinet latch or lock where these products are stored.
Consider traditional liquid or powder detergent instead of single-load packets while children 6 or younger live in or visit the home.
Save Poison Help (1-800-222-1222) in your phone and call it if a child gets detergent in the mouth or eyes.

reminder.text: Check that laundry packets and cleaners are back in the high, locked spot.

verify_rule: All laundry packets and cleaning products are in a closed, high or locked cabinet in original containers, not within a child's reach.
blind_spots: Products inside closed cabinets or the garage
Spray bottles and sink-side items outside the frame
Homes of relatives and other caregivers
